chapter: Heroes, rivals and the drummers' craft
title: Recognising drummers by sound and Sonny Greer's flashy style
summary: Crawford says he could identify drummers by sound and that Sonny Greer had a distinctive sound but was suited only to Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And like now, could you tell -- like say, if you came into a place and you couldn't see who the drummer was, could you tell by the sound that the drummers have, the individual sound?
Pretty much I could tell, because that's all I went to listen for was the drummer.

Well, what did -- now, did you -- you wre saying the thing about Sonny Greer. Did you -- I don't know. Like certain drummers have told me that they thought that Sonny Greer just couldn't play, that he was in the band because Duke was (inaudible), he was a friend of Duke's.
Well, he was merely primarily a Duke

Ellington band player. Put him in another bunch, another band, uh-uh. He played, but Sonny had a different sound on his drum that you could just readily hear. And then you say, oh, that sounds like Sonny Greer.
Yeah, well, I noticed this too. A lot of the older recordings, a lot of the times he wasn't really playing time, you know. He would be --
You know, the bass player would be playing the time, and Sonny would be --
-- yeah, he'd be playing a lot --
Yeah, it was a difference. Chick Webb was the greatest.
